# Log

## 2026-06-28 — Initial build (5 sources ingested)

Created the BioOKF bundle **07 Neuromuscular Neuro** and ingested all sources from
`benchmark_corpus/07_neuromuscular_neuro/papers/`.

**Sources ingested into `raw/` (5):**
- PMID 25755201 — Mayer et al. 2015, *Characterization of pulmonary function in DMD* (Pediatr Pulmonol).
- PMID 9014949 — Hahn et al. 1997, *Clinical implications of maximal respiratory pressures in DMD* (Arch Phys Med Rehabil).
- PMID 34400559 — Topaloudi et al. 2022, *Myasthenia gravis GWAS implicates AGRN* (J Med Genet).
- PMID 36596294 — Levine et al. 2023, *Pulmonary function tests for evaluating DMD severity* (Acta Paediatr).
- PMID 38355534 — 2024, *EURO-NMD registry: federated FAIR infrastructure* (Orphanet J Rare Dis).

**Graph:** 134 concept documents, 371 edges, 0 parse errors. `bokf verify` = ok (0 errors).

**By node type:** Disease 19, BiomedicalMeasure 16, Molecule 15, Gene 13, MethodOrProcedure 13,
Phenotype 13, Study 8, Dataset 7, Agent 6, Anatomy 6, Variant 7, Publication 5, Concept 3,
MolecularClass 1, Device 1, Organism 1.

**What each source contributed:**
- *DMD respiratory (Mayer 2015, Hahn 1997, Levine 2023):* a shared spine around `duchenne-muscular-dystrophy`,
  `dmd-gene`/`dystrophin`, respiratory-muscle weakness, the PFT measures (FVC, PEF, PCF, MIP, MEP, TLC,
  RV, VC, ERV, IRV, FRC, transcutaneous/arterial CO2, CK), procedures (spirometry, PFT, mechanical
  ventilation, cough assistance), glucocorticoids + mutation-specific drugs, and the ATS / modified-ATS
  criteria. Quantified edges carry annual decline rates, correlations and p-values.
- *MG GWAS (Topaloudi 2022):* `myasthenia-gravis` (+ EOMG/LOMG/CMS), 12 risk genes (AGRN, TNFRSF11A,
  CTLA4, ISG15, HLA-DRB1/DQA1/B, SRCAP, FBRS, TNIP1, PTPN22, ZBTB10), 7 variants with OR/p, the
  agrin–LRP4–MuSK–AChR NMJ axis, autoantibodies, methods (GWAS, HLA fine-mapping, LDSC) and genetic
  correlation with T1D/RA/ATD/late-onset vitiligo.
- *EURO-NMD registry (2024):* the registry/hub, EURO-NMD ERN, three patient organisations, the five
  disease groups, ontologies (HPO, ORDO, OMIM, HGVS), REDCap/FAIR Data Point/federated query, FAIR
  principles, and four interoperable pilot registries.

**Negative findings captured as `not_*` edges:** peak-cough-flow not_associated_with loss-of-ambulation;
glucocorticoids not_associated_with FVC (Mayer/Levine cohorts); PTPN22 not_predisposes_to EOMG; ZBTB10
not_predisposes_to LOMG.

**Open backfill (14 `source.unanchored` warnings, non-blocking):** ancillary entities that are mentioned
but not ingested as sources (patient organisations, the UDP & CINRG cohorts, the four pilot registries,
the EU/NMD/DS common-data-element layers, ATS) — `xref`/anchors can be added later.

abdominal-muscles.body:
# Abdominal muscles

Early and prominent abdominal-muscle weakness explains why MEP declines before MIP in DMD and
other neuromuscular disorders.

stats.quote: weakness of abdominal muscles, which plays an important role during forced expiration and coughing

extra.definition: Expiratory muscles essential for forced expiration and coughing; their early weakness in neuromuscular disease is reflected in reduced MEP.

acetylcholine-receptor.body:
# Acetylcholine receptor (AChR)

Pathogenic anti-AChR antibodies are found in up to 85% of MG cases; agrin-LRP4-MuSK signalling
drives AChR clustering, and agrin-knockout mice show fewer, smaller AChR clusters.

stats.quote: the formation of AChR clusters in the postsynaptic membrane

extra.definition: The skeletal-muscle nicotinic acetylcholine receptor (AChR); the principal autoantigen in myasthenia gravis, clustered on the postsynaptic membrane.

afm-telethon.body:

AFM-Telethon is one of three patient organisations that co-funded the EURO-NMD Registry Hub and contributed in-kind support (a shared contribution of 274,641.20 euros across the three organisations). As an equal partner with co-governance rights, it helped ensure the registry is patient-centred, meaningful and impactful.

agrin.body:
# Agrin

A critical organiser of postsynaptic differentiation. Anti-agrin autoantibodies occur in
seropositive and seronegative MG, and immunising mice with agrin induces MG-like symptoms.

stats.quote: Agrin ... is an LRP4 interaction partner that mediates the activation of MuSK
mediates the activation of MuSK and the formation of AChR clusters in the postsynaptic membrane
mediating MuSK activation and subsequent AChR clustering
the formation of AChR clusters in the postsynaptic membrane

extra.definition: A heparan-sulfate proteoglycan that, by binding LRP4 and activating MuSK, drives acetylcholine- receptor clustering and synaptic stabilisation at the neuromuscular junction.

agrn.body:
# AGRN

On chromosome 1p36.33, 5.58 kb downstream of ISG15. The independent intronic SNP rs3128125
underlies its MG association. The first MG risk gene encoding an NMJ-organising protein.

stats.quote: AGRN encodes the proteoglycan agrin involved in the activation and synaptic stabilisation of the NMJ
gene-based analysis revealed AGRN as a novel MG susceptibility gene
mutations in AGRN are a rare cause of congenital myasthenic syndrome characterised by fatigable weakness of skeletal muscle

extra.definition: The agrin gene on 1p36.33; newly implicated as a myasthenia gravis susceptibility gene and the first MG risk locus encoding a protein (agrin) directly relevant to neuromuscular-junction activation.

american-thoracic-society.body:
# American Thoracic Society (ATS)

Standard ATS spirometry acceptability criteria are designed to maximise expiratory flow for
obstructive-disease testing and are considered overly restrictive for DMD.

extra.definition: The American Thoracic Society (ATS); issues spirometry acceptability and standardisation guidelines, which Mayer 2015 modified for neuromuscular disease.

anti-achr-antibody.body:
# Anti-AChR antibody

Detected by radioimmunoassay (positive >= 0.5 nmol/L); the cohort excluded anti-MuSK and
anti-LRP4 cases and selected for anti-AChR positivity.

stats.quote: Pathogenic autoantibodies against the skeletal muscle acetylcholine receptor (AChR) are detected in up to 85% of MG cases
mediated by autoantibodies that target the postsynaptic proteins of the neuromuscular junction

extra.definition: Autoantibody against the skeletal-muscle acetylcholine receptor; the principal pathogenic and diagnostic autoantibody in myasthenia gravis (up to 85% of cases).

anti-agrin-antibody.body:
# Anti-agrin antibody

Agrin is a recent addition to the MG autoantigen list; immunising mice with agrin induces MG-like
symptoms, supporting a pathogenic role.

stats.quote: Antiagrin autoantibodies have been detected in seropositive as well as seronegative patients with MG
Antiagrin autoantibodies have been detected in seropositive as well as seronegative patients with MG

extra.definition: Autoantibody against agrin; detected in seropositive and seronegative MG, with anti-agrin immunisation inducing MG-like disease in mice.

anti-lrp4-antibody.body:
# Anti-LRP4 antibody

Part of the expanding autoantibody spectrum of MG; anti-LRP4 cases were excluded from the novel
Greek/Greek-Cypriot sample.

stats.quote: antibodies against the lipoprotein-receptor-related protein 4 (LRP4) ... have been detected in double-seronegative and seropositive MG cases
antibodies against the lipoprotein-receptor-related protein 4 (LRP4)

extra.definition: Autoantibody against LRP4; detected in double-seronegative and seropositive MG patients.

anti-musk-antibody.body:
# Anti-MuSK antibody

Anti-MuSK MG cases were excluded from the Greek/Greek-Cypriot sample, which was restricted to
anti-AChR-positive MG.

stats.quote: autoantibodies may be directed against the muscle-specific receptor tyrosine kinase (MuSK) in up to 10% of patients
autoantibodies may be directed against the muscle-specific receptor tyrosine kinase (MuSK)

extra.definition: Autoantibody against muscle-specific kinase (MuSK); found in up to 10% of MG patients, defining a distinct seropositive subgroup.

arterial-pco2.body:
# Arterial PaCO2

Wake PaCO2 correlated logarithmically with MIP; hypercapnia (>6 kPa) appeared once MIP fell
below ~30 cmH2O, identifying inspiratory weakness as sufficient to cause ventilatory failure.

stats.quote: elevation of wake Paco2 as an indication of impending or manifest respiratory insufficiency

extra.definition: Arterial carbon-dioxide tension (PaCO2); wake elevation indicates impending or manifest ventilatory insufficiency in DMD.

ataluren.body:
# Ataluren

A mutation-specific (nonsense-mutation readthrough) DMD therapy; given to 4 of 62 patients in
Levine 2023.

stats.quote: Ataluren (Transelerna)

extra.definition: A nonsense-mutation readthrough agent (Translarna) used as a mutation-specific DMD therapy.

autoimmune-thyroid-disease.body:
# Autoimmune thyroid disease (ATD)

Genetically correlated with MG (rg=0.29, p=0.0073); thyroiditis is a classic polyautoimmune and
familial-autoimmune association of MG.

extra.definition: Autoimmune thyroid disease (e.g. thyroiditis, Graves'); a frequent MG comorbidity and genetically correlated with MG.

becker-muscular-dystrophy.body:
# Becker muscular dystrophy (BMD)

Allelic to DMD; because DNA/dystrophin testing was not done systematically in the Hahn 1997
cohort, severe BMD patients may have been included among the DMD group.

stats.quote: severe Becker muscular dystrophy patients may have been included
MEP has been found to be more severely affected than MIP in Becker muscular dystrophy

extra.definition: Milder allelic dystrophinopathy to DMD; in its severe form clinically overlapping with DMD, with maximal expiratory pressure (MEP) more severely affected than inspiratory (MIP).

bulbar-weakness.body:
# Bulbar weakness

Bulbar and limb muscle weakness are typical clinical manifestations of MG alongside ocular ptosis
and diplopia.

extra.definition: Weakness of bulbar (cranial-nerve-innervated) muscles affecting speech, chewing and swallowing; a typical manifestation of myasthenia gravis.

cinrg-dnhs.body:
# CINRG Duchenne Natural History Study

A large longitudinal DMD study; Levine 2023 contrasts its findings (glucocorticoid association
with higher PEF/MIP/MEP; FVC correlated with upper-extremity function) with their own.

stats.quote: the Cooperative International Neuromuscular Research Group Duchenne Natural History Study, demonstrated a correlation between FVC and the loss of upper extremity function

extra.definition: The Cooperative International Neuromuscular Research Group (CINRG) Duchenne Natural History Study; a longitudinal DMD cohort characterising pulmonary-function outcomes with and without glucocorticoids.

congenital-myasthenic-syndrome.body:
# Congenital myasthenic syndrome (CMS)

A genetic NMJ disorder distinct from autoimmune MG; the shared AGRN involvement links the
inherited and autoimmune ends of the NMJ-disease spectrum.

stats.quote: mutations in AGRN are a rare cause of congenital myasthenic syndrome
congenital myasthenic syndrome characterised by fatigable weakness of skeletal muscle

extra.definition: A genetic (non-autoimmune) disorder of neuromuscular transmission causing fatigable skeletal-muscle weakness; rarely caused by AGRN mutations.

cough-assist-device.body:
# Cough-assist device

Used within cough-assistance therapy; indicated by guideline PCF/FVC/MEP thresholds, though
Levine 2023 cautions against PCF as the sole trigger.

stats.quote: Treatment for improving mucous drainage and pulmonary ventilation in DMD consists of respiratory physiotherapy and the use of a cough assist device

extra.definition: A mechanical insufflation-exsufflation device that augments cough and clears airway secretions in neuromuscular disease.

cough-assistance.body:
# Cough assistance

Guideline indications to begin cough assistance: FVC < 50% predicted, PCF < 270 L/min and
MEP < 60 cmH2O, or PCF < 160 L/min; 2018 guidelines recommend earlier initiation.

stats.quote: Internationally accepted guidelines for treating DMD delineate indications to begin cough assistance

extra.definition: Assisted-cough therapy (with a cough-assist device) plus respiratory physiotherapy to clear secretions when cough is impaired in DMD.

creatine-kinase.body:
# Creatine kinase (CK)

A markedly elevated CK is part of the clinical DMD case definition alongside early symptom
onset, Gowers' sign and a confirmed dystrophin mutation.

stats.quote: DMD was defined clinically as onset of symptoms by age 5, a positive Gowers' sign, abnormal gait pattern, markedly elevated creatine kinase level

extra.definition: Serum creatine kinase (CK); markedly elevated in DMD as a marker of muscle-membrane damage and part of the clinical diagnosis.

ctla4.body:
# CTLA4

A T-cell checkpoint regulator previously linked to MG and many autoimmune diseases; significant
in the gene-based MG meta-analysis (rs231770), though it did not pass the LOMG threshold.

stats.quote: four genes, TNFRSF11A, CTLA4, AGRN and ISG15, were found significantly associated with MG

extra.definition: Cytotoxic T-lymphocyte-associated protein 4 on 2q33.2; an immune-checkpoint gene associated with myasthenia gravis.

deflazacort.body:
# Deflazacort

Associated with higher FVC% than prednisone in prior work, though Levine 2023 could not confirm

diagnostic-odyssey.body:

The diagnostic odyssey is the phenomenon whereby rare disease patients, including those with neuromuscular disorders that are challenging to recognise, experience long diagnosis delays. The EURO-NMD Network and Registry work to speed up diagnosis and reduce this delay, tracking it through KPIs such as time to diagnosis.

stats.quote: Neuromuscular disorders are challenging to recognise, and patients experience long diagnosis delays, a phenomenon coined the "diagnostic odyssey".
patients experience long diagnosis delays, a phenomenon coined the "diagnostic odyssey".

extra.definition: The "diagnostic odyssey" is the phenomenon of long diagnosis delays experienced by patients with rare diseases, including neuromuscular disorders, which the EURO-NMD Registry aims to reduce.

diaphragm.body:
# Diaphragm

Hahn 1997 inferred relative early sparing of the diaphragm, since MIP (inspiratory strength)
is preserved until ~13 years while MEP declines earlier.

stats.quote: progressive respiratory muscle failure, in particular the diaphragm

extra.definition: The principal inspiratory muscle; relatively spared early in DMD but progressively weakened, contributing to restrictive ventilatory failure.

diplopia.body:
# Diplopia

A typical ocular manifestation of MG reflecting fatigable extraocular-muscle weakness.

extra.definition: Double vision from impaired extraocular-muscle coordination; a typical ocular symptom of myasthenia gravis.

duchenne-muscular-dystrophy.body:
# Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD)

X-linked recessive dystrophinopathy, globally affecting ~1:5000 newborn males. Diagnosed
clinically by symptom onset before age 5, a positive Gowers' sign, abnormal gait, markedly
elevated creatine kinase and loss of ambulation by age 12, with a confirmed dystrophin
mutation. Respiratory insufficiency from progressive respiratory-muscle weakness drives a
restrictive ventilatory defect and is a leading cause of morbidity and mortality.

stats.quote: Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy (DMD, OMIM 310200) is the most common neuromuscular disorder of childhood
Respiratory insufficiency in DMD is caused by progressive respiratory muscle failure, in particular the diaphragm, which leads to restrictive respiratory disease
progressive respiratory muscle weakness is a major factor in the development of respiratory insufficiency
deficiency in dystrophin protein leads to progressive skeletal muscle atrophy
This causes weakness, loss of ambulation and motor skills
it can also be influenced by scoliosis especially in nonambulatory DMD patients
A continuously progressive restrictive pulmonary syndrome becomes apparent by 10 to 12 years of age

extra.definition: The most common neuromuscular disorder of childhood; an X-linked recessive dystrophinopathy caused by DMD mutations and dystrophin deficiency, producing progressive skeletal-muscle atrophy, loss of ambulation and ultimately respiratory and cardiac failure (death typically in the third decade).

dystrophin.body:
# Dystrophin

Deficiency of dystrophin in DMD causes premature muscle cell failure, progressive muscle
atrophy, weakness and loss of ambulation.

stats.quote: a deficiency in dystrophin protein causes premature muscle cell failure and leads to progressive muscle atrophy

extra.definition: Large sarcolemmal cytoskeletal protein encoded by DMD; its deficiency causes premature muscle-cell failure and progressive muscular dystrophy.

early-onset-myasthenia-gravis.body:
# Early-onset myasthenia gravis (EOMG)

SNP heritability ~0.27. Its genome-wide signal is dominated by the HLA region; HLA-B*08:01/HLA-B*08
is the only independent classic-allele locus (OR 3.24). A novel association maps between SRCAP and
FBRS.

stats.quote: in early-onset MG (EOMG; <50 years old) a female predominance is evident

extra.definition: Anti-AChR MG with age at onset < 50 years; female-predominant, and genetically driven mainly by the HLA-B*08:01 / HLA-B*08 haplotype.

ejp-rd-virtual-platform.body:
# EJP-RD Virtual Platform

The EJP-RD Virtual Platform, developed by the European Joint Programme on Rare Diseases, facilitates querying of the EURO-NMD Registry and Registry Hub. It offers a graphical user interface for humans and an API for computers to query data across existing registries, working only when the data exposed by registries are FAIR so that data stay at the source but remain queryable at a distance. EJP-RD also developed the semantic model for the EU common data elements used to achieve interoperability.

an Application Programming Interface (API) for computers to query data across existing registries and the registry hub.
this can only be possible when the data exposed by various registries are FAIR, where data stay at the source but can be queryable at a distance from an EJP-RD query point.
the semantic model for the EU-CDEs developed by EJPRD (European Joint Programme on Rare Diseases).

extra.definition: The EJP-RD Virtual Platform is a federated query infrastructure developed by the European Joint Programme on Rare Diseases, offering a GUI for humans and an API for computers to query FAIR data across existing registries and the EURO-NMD Registry Hub without moving data.

An exon-skipping antisense-oligonucleotide DMD therapy; given to 7 of 62 patients in Levine 2023.

eu-common-data-elements.body:
# EU Common Data Elements (EU-CDEs)

The EU Common Data Elements are a dataset of 16 common data elements for rare disease registration defined by the Joint Research Centre of the European Commission, freely available in 21 languages. They are the first practical EU instrument for increasing interoperability of rare disease registries, are mandated across all ERN registries enabling cross-ERN comparisons, and form the base layer of the EURO-NMD Registry's three-tiered dataset model.

stats.quote: The registry has three-layered datasets, with European Commission-mandated data elements (EU-CDEs).
The Joint Research Centre (JRC) of the European Commission has defined a "Set of common data elements for Rare Diseases Registration".
This dataset of 16 common data elements, the EU-CDEs, is freely available on the internet in 21 languages.

extra.definition: The EU Common Data Elements (EU-CDEs) are a set of 16 common data elements for rare disease registration defined by the Joint Research Centre of the European Commission, mandated across ERN registries and forming the base layer of the EURO-NMD Registry's three-layered datasets.

euro-nmd.body:
# EURO-NMD (European Reference Network for Rare Neuromuscular Diseases)

EURO-NMD is the European Reference Network for rare neuromuscular diseases, which collectively affect about 500,000 EU citizens. One of the largest ERNs, it brings together 82 healthcare providers across 25 European countries and 27 patient organisations, and is structured around five disease groups: Muscle Diseases, Peripheral Nerve Diseases, Neuromuscular Junction Defects, Mitochondrial Diseases and Motor Neuron Diseases. It works to speed up diagnosis and research and operates the EURO-NMD Registry.

stats.quote: EURO-NMD is the European Reference Network for Rare Neuromuscular Diseases, collectively affecting 500,000 EU citizens.
EURO-NMD is one the largest ERNs bringing together 82 healthcare providers across 25 European countries and including 27 patient organisations.

extra.definition: EURO-NMD is the European Reference Network for Rare Neuromuscular Diseases, bringing together 82 healthcare providers across 25 European countries and 27 patient organisations, structured around five main disease groups, and operating the EURO-NMD Registry.

euro-nmd-registry.body:
# EURO-NMD Registry

The EURO-NMD Registry is the patient-centred clinical registry of the European Reference Network for rare neuromuscular diseases. It collects clinical, neuromuscular imaging, histopathology, biological and genetic data and patient-reported outcomes in a computer-interpretable format using selected ontologies. The registry is housed within the secure hospital IT infrastructure of University Medical Centre Freiburg, uses an opt-in, GDPR-compliant, pseudonymised hybrid model, and is implemented in REDCap with five disease-driven datasets plus an undiagnosed-patient branch. It forms a component of the wider EURO-NMD Registry Hub and was FAIR-by-design, scoring 19 of 22 on the FAIR Evaluator.

stats.quote: The EURO-NMD Registry collects data from all neuromuscular patients seen at EURO-NMD's expert centres.
The EURO-NMD registry is a component of the Hub that addresses the data collection needs of the healthcare providers that are members of the ERN.
EURO-NMD is the European Reference Network for Rare Neuromuscular Diseases, collectively affecting 500,000 EU citizens.
Data from the EURO-NMD Registry will be collected and managed using Research Electronic Data Capture (REDCap) software hosted at University Medical Center Freiburg.
All data elements and their hierarchical dependencies are described in the codebook and adopt standard ontologies as recommended for data integration.
the system will return a list of codes from the Orphanet Rare Disease Ontology (ORDO) for selection.
OMIM | Classification of genes and diseases | https://www.omim.org
we adopted a nomenclature compliant with Human Genome Variation Society (HGVS) recommendations.
the FAIR-by-design EURO-NMD registry has built-in interoperability founded on using accepted ontologies and classifications.
EURO-NMD registry: federated FAIR infrastructure, innovative technologies and concepts of a patient-centred registry for rare neuromuscular disorders.

extra.definition: The EURO-NMD Registry is a patient-centred, FAIR-by-design clinical registry that collects longitudinal clinical, imaging, histopathology, biological, genetic and patient-reported data from all neuromuscular patients seen at EURO-NMD expert centres. It is housed in the secure IT infrastructure of University Medical Centre Freiburg and implemented in REDCap.

euro-nmd-registry-hub.body:
# EURO-NMD Registry Hub

The EURO-NMD Registry Hub is the federating framework that connects the EURO-NMD Registry with other neuromuscular data sources via an interoperability layer and FAIR Data Points. Launched in May 2020 with co-funding from the EU 3rd Health Programme and three patient organisations (World Duchenne Organisation, Duchenne Data Foundation, AFM-Telethon), it enables GDPR-compliant, privacy-preserving federated analysis across siloed registries so that data never leaves its source.

stats.quote: the Registry Hub brings together data that are currently siloed and fragmented to improve healthcare and advance research for neuromuscular diseases.
