euro-nmd-registry-paper-2024.body:
# EURO-NMD Registry Paper (2024)

The source publication, "EURO-NMD registry: federated FAIR infrastructure, innovative technologies and concepts of a patient-centred registry for rare neuromuscular disorders," appeared in Orphanet Journal of Rare Diseases in 2024 (PMID 38355534). It describes the design, datasets, IT architecture, ontologies, governance and FAIR interoperability of the EURO-NMD Registry and Registry Hub.

stats.quote: EURO-NMD registry: federated FAIR infrastructure, innovative technologies and concepts of a patient-centred registry for rare neuromuscular disorders.

extra.definition: Peer-reviewed article in Orphanet Journal of Rare Diseases (2024) describing the EURO-NMD Registry and Registry Hub, its federated FAIR infrastructure, datasets, ontologies, governance and patient-centred design.

european-commission.body:
# European Commission

The European Commission funds and oversees the activities of the European Reference Networks, including the EURO-NMD Registry, which it requires as an essential vector for monitoring homogeneous care delivery. It co-funded the EURO-NMD Registry Hub through the EU 3rd Health Programme, and its Joint Research Centre (JRC) defined the EU common data elements for rare disease registration.

stats.quote: The EURO-NMD Registry is an essential vector within the European Reference Networks' activities required by the European Commission, which funds and oversees the different network activities.
The Joint Research Centre (JRC) of the European Commission has defined a "Set of common data elements for Rare Diseases Registration".
the EU Health Programme has allocated funds so ERNs can develop registries with mixed clinical monitoring and research purposes.

extra.definition: The European Commission funds and oversees the European Reference Networks and co-funded the EURO-NMD Registry Hub through the EU 3rd Health Programme; its Joint Research Centre defined the EU common data elements for rare disease registration.

expiratory-reserve-volume.body:
# Expiratory reserve volume (ERV)

ERV declines with expiratory-muscle (MEP) weakness; together with rising RV this drives much of
the intrathoracic volume loss seen between ages 12 and 16 in DMD.

stats.quote: Declines in MEP also correlated linearly with expiratory reserve volume (p < .001)

extra.definition: The additional volume that can be exhaled below tidal expiration (ERV); falls with expiratory-muscle weakness in DMD.

fair-data-point.body:
# FAIR Data Point

A FAIR Data Point is a metadata repository designed to adhere to as many FAIR principles as possible. It follows the Data Catalog Vocabulary (DCAT) standard and adds the machine-actionable read/write behaviours of the Linked Data Platform, registering itself in a central index for smart search. In the EURO-NMD Registry Hub, transformed interoperability data is hosted in a triplestore as a component of a FAIR Data Point, acting as a gateway that describes access conditions and enables federation across registries.

stats.quote: hosting this transformed data in a triplestore, which is a component of a FAIR Data Point.
data from rare neuromuscular patients across different platforms linked through FAIR Data Points.
A FAIR Data Point (FDP) is "a metadata repository specifically designed to adhere to as many FAIR Principles and norms as possible."
FDPs also automatically register themselves in a central index ... making this software an indispensable component of a FAIRification process.

extra.definition: A FAIR Data Point (FDP) is a metadata repository designed to adhere to FAIR principles, following the DCAT standard and Linked Data Platform behaviours, used in the EURO-NMD Registry Hub to expose datasets in a FAIR, machine-actionable manner and enable federation across registries.

fair-evaluator.body:
# FAIR Evaluator

The FAIR Evaluator is an open-source automated evaluation system that measures how well a resource conforms to the FAIR principles across 22 individual tests. It was used to assess the newly built EURO-NMD Registry, which scored 19 of 22 points, failing only R1.3 (conformance of metadata to community standards). The assessment helped guide development teams and provided proof of compliance with FAIRness requirements set by the EURO-NMD Steering Committee.

stats.quote: A FAIR assessment of the newly-built EURO-NMD registry was achieved using an automated evaluation system called the 'FAIR Evaluator', developed as an open source.
The EURO-NMD registry scored 19 out of 22 possible points, representing 22 individual tests spanning all FAIR principles except for R1.3.
an automated evaluation system called the 'FAIR Evaluator', developed as an open source (https://w3id.org/AmIFAIR).

extra.definition: The FAIR Evaluator is an open-source automated evaluation system that assesses how well a resource conforms to the FAIR principles through individual tests; it was used to assess the EURO-NMD Registry, which scored 19 of 22 points.

fair-principles.body:
# FAIR Principles

FAIR is the acronym for a global initiative to make data more valuable by increasing the ability of computers to find, interpret, integrate and analyse data autonomously: Findable, Accessible, Interoperable and Reusable. The EURO-NMD Registry was built FAIR-by-design, registered in the JRC ERDRI platform for findability, and scored 19 of 22 on the FAIR Evaluator (failing only R1.3, conformance to community standards).

stats.quote: the FAIR-by-design and strong patient engagement in design and implementation are two innovative pillars of our registry platform.
FAIR stands for Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, and Reusable.

extra.definition: The FAIR principles describe a global initiative to make data Findable, Accessible, Interoperable and Reusable, increasing the ability of computers to find, interpret, integrate and analyse data autonomously; the EURO-NMD Registry was built FAIR-by-design.

fatigable-muscle-weakness.body:
# Fatigable muscle weakness

The defining clinical feature distinguishing NMJ-transmission disorders from the fixed, progressive
weakness of dystrophinopathies.

extra.definition: Muscle weakness that worsens with sustained or repeated activity; the hallmark of neuromuscular-junction disorders (myasthenia gravis, congenital myasthenic syndrome).

fbrs.body:
# FBRS

Neighbours SRCAP on 16p11.2; the independent EOMG SNP rs8058928 lies in the SRCAP/LOC730183/FBRS
intergenic region.

stats.quote: three neighbouring genes, namely SRCAP, LOC730183 and FBRS, were significantly associated

extra.definition: Fibrosin (FBRS) on 16p11.2, neighbouring SRCAP; part of the novel early-onset MG association region.

federated-query.body:
# Federated Query (Data Visiting)

Federated query, also called the "data visiting" approach, is the data-sharing method underpinning the EURO-NMD Registry Hub. Queries run on demand over distributed FAIR datasets without any data transfer between registries; data stay at the source and only aggregated or anonymised answers (such as patient counts) are returned, protected by a proxy and encrypted communication. The approach was demonstrated across four pilot registries and is enabled by shared ontologies and the EJP-RD Virtual Platform.

stats.quote: a data-sharing model relying on federated queries that run without data transfer between registries ('the data visiting' approach).
It is now possible to conduct the same queries related to neuromuscular diseases in multiple independent registries simultaneously without exposing sensitive patient details.
FAIR makes it possible for the same query to be executed over independent resources; thus, sharing those queries leads to convergence between registries.
the federated queries run on distributed agents containing just enough aggregated or anonymised data to answer the questions.

extra.definition: Federated query (the "data visiting" approach) is a data-sharing method in which queries run over distributed FAIR datasets without transferring data between registries, returning only aggregated or anonymised answers and preserving patient privacy.

forced-vital-capacity.body:
# Forced vital capacity (FVC)

Percent-predicted FVC declines near-linearly (~5%/year, Mayer 2015; ~3.8%/year in
non-ambulatory patients, Levine 2023) and best correlates with lung-volume loss and
ambulation, making it the central severity outcome in DMD trials.

stats.quote: The percent predicted, FVC and PEF showed a near linear decline of approximately 5% points/year from ages 5 to 24
PFT values were lower for %FVC ... (p < 0.01 for all)

extra.definition: The volume of air forcibly exhaled after maximal inspiration (FVC); the most-used spirometric outcome for tracking restrictive lung disease and disease severity in DMD.

functional-residual-capacity.body:
# Functional residual capacity (FRC)

Part of the thoracic-volume panel; elevated FRC with low MEP places advanced DMD patients close
to the inspiratory-muscle fatigue threshold.

stats.quote: Functional residual capacity (FRC) was measured by helium dilution technique

extra.definition: The volume remaining in the lungs at the end of a normal tidal expiration (FRC); measured by helium dilution in Hahn 1997.

genome-wide-association-study.body:
# Genome-wide association study (GWAS)

Combined with gene-based analysis (MAGMA), conditional analysis (GCTA-COJO), HLA fine-mapping and
LD-score regression to map MG risk loci and onset-specific architecture.

stats.quote: we investigate the genetic architecture of MG via a genome-wide association study (GWAS)

extra.definition: A study design testing millions of SNPs for association with a trait; used here in a meta-analysis of 1401 MG cases and 3508 controls (5,755,778 SNPs).

glucocorticoids.body:
# Glucocorticoids

Standard of care in DMD via anti-inflammatory preservation of muscle strength. Notably, both
Mayer 2015 and Levine 2023 found no difference in pulmonary function (FVC/PEF) by steroid use in
their cohorts, despite established long-term benefit; side effects include growth failure,
weight gain and osteoporosis.

stats.quote: Corticosteroid treatment has been shown to modify the natural progression of the disease by slowing the decline of motor and pulmonary function, and extending survival
no difference was observed in FVC or PEF by ambulation or steroid treatment

extra.definition: Corticosteroid drug class (prednisone/prednisolone, deflazacort, vamorolone); the standard of care in DMD, slowing motor and pulmonary decline and prolonging ambulation and survival.

gowers-sign.body:
# Gowers' sign

A positive Gowers' sign is part of the clinical DMD definition used in the United
Dystrophinopathy Project cohort (onset by age 5, positive Gowers' sign, abnormal gait,
elevated CK, loss of ambulation by 12).

extra.definition: Use of the hands to "climb up" the legs when rising from the floor, indicating proximal lower-limb weakness; a classic clinical sign of DMD.

hahn-1997-respiratory-pressures-dmd.body:
# Hahn 1997 — Maximal respiratory pressures in DMD

Inception cohort of 52 consecutive DMD patients. Found expiratory muscle weakness (MEP)
appears first and declines linearly with age, while inspiratory muscle weakness (MIP)
best predicts hypercapnia (appearing when MIP < 30 cmH2O). Lung-volume changes correlate
with respiratory-muscle weakness.

extra.definition: Hahn A, Bach JR, Delaubier A, et al. (1997), Arch Phys Med Rehabil 78:1-6, "Clinical Implications of Maximal Respiratory Pressure Determinations for Individuals With Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy" — inception cohort of 52 DMD patients correlating MIP, MEP, lung volumes and arterial PaCO2.

helium-dilution-technique.body:
# Helium-dilution technique

Used in Hahn 1997 to derive VC, TV, IRV, ERV, RV and TLC; not feasible in 10 subjects with
insufficient pulmonary function.

stats.quote: Functional residual capacity (FRC) was measured by helium dilution technique using a 9-liter closed circuit helium-residual apparatus

extra.definition: A closed-circuit helium-dilution method for measuring functional residual capacity and derived static lung volumes.

hgvs-nomenclature.body:
# HGVS Nomenclature

The Human Genome Variation Society (HGVS) nomenclature is the standard for annotating genetic modifications at the chromosomal, gene, variant and protein level. The EURO-NMD Registry adopted an HGVS-compliant nomenclature for annotating the exact genetic defect, which is essential for many rare diseases.

stats.quote: we adopted a nomenclature compliant with Human Genome Variation Society (HGVS) recommendations.
Human genome variation society | Annotation of modification at chromosomal, gene, variant and protein level | https://www.hgvs.org/

extra.definition: The Human Genome Variation Society (HGVS) nomenclature is a standard for annotating sequence variants at the chromosomal, gene, variant and protein level, adopted by the EURO-NMD Registry for genetic variant annotation.

hla-b.body:
# HLA-B

The HLA-B*08:01/HLA-B*08 haplotype is the dominant, strongly predisposing classic allele in EOMG
(OR 3.24); in the joint analysis HLA-B is independent of HLA-DRB1.

stats.quote: In the HLA-B region, rs1131215 showed the strongest association (p=4.87x10-9, OR=1.32)
HLA-B*08:01 and HLA-B*08 (r2=1) had the strongest association (p=2.69x10-37, OR=3.24)

extra.definition: HLA class I B on 6p21.33; one of two independent HLA loci in MG overall and the only independent HLA locus in early-onset MG.

hla-b-08-01.body:
# HLA-B*08:01

The strongest classic-allele association in EOMG (OR 3.24), consistent with prior studies of
early-onset MG.

stats.quote: HLA-B was found to be the only independent locus; HLA-B*08:01 and HLA-B*08 (r2=1) had the strongest association
HLA-B*08:01 and HLA-B*08 (r2=1) had the strongest association (p=2.69x10-37, OR=3.24)

extra.definition: The HLA-B*08:01/HLA-B*08 classic allele; the dominant predisposing locus in early-onset myasthenia gravis.

hla-dqa1.body:
# HLA-DQA1

rs34481484 (HLA-DQA1) was the top and single genome-wide-significant HLA SNP in the joint MG
meta-analysis; the LOMG top variant rs9271539 lies between HLA-DQA1 and HLA-DRB1.

stats.quote: An additional significantly associated locus was identified in the HLA-DQA1 gene (rs34481484; p=3.72x10-9, OR=2.11)

extra.definition: HLA class II alpha chain DQA1 on 6p21.32; carries the top genome-wide-significant HLA SNP in the overall MG meta-analysis.

stats.quote: we identified two associated loci, HLA-DRB1 and HLA-B ... HLA-DRB1*13:01 was the most strongly associated allele (p=2.6x10-9, OR=0.47)
Focusing on LOMG, HLA-DRB1 was detected as the only independent locus

extra.definition: HLA class II beta chain DRB1 on 6p21.32; one of two independent HLA loci underlying MG, and the only independent HLA locus in LOMG.

hla-drb1-03-01.body:
# HLA-DRB1*03:01

Protective in LOMG (OR 0.47); conditional analysis showed DRB1*03:01 and DRB1*13:01 as the two
independent protective alleles in HLA-DRB1.

stats.quote: HLA-DRB1*03:01 was the most strongly associated classic allele with a protective role against MG

extra.definition: The HLA-DRB1*03:01 classic allele; the most strongly associated (protective) allele in late-onset myasthenia gravis.

hla-drb1-13-01.body:
# HLA-DRB1*13:01

Protective against MG (OR 0.47) in both EOMG and LOMG; the same allele is protective in
anti-citrullinated-protein-antibody-positive rheumatoid arthritis.

stats.quote: Within the HLA-DRB1 region, HLA-DRB1*13:01 was the most strongly associated allele
HLA-DRB1*13:01 was the most strongly associated allele (p=2.6x10-9, OR=0.47)

extra.definition: The HLA-DRB1*13:01 classic allele; the strongest protective allele in the joint MG HLA analysis.

hla-fine-mapping.body:
# HLA fine-mapping

Resolved two independent MG loci (HLA-DRB1 and HLA-B); HLA-B drives EOMG, HLA-DRB1 drives LOMG.

stats.quote: we proceeded with fine-mapping efforts. Classic HLA alleles and SNPs were imputed for further examination

extra.definition: Imputation and association testing of classic HLA alleles and SNPs (here via SNP2HLA) to resolve independent HLA signals within the complex MHC LD structure.

human-phenotype-ontology.body:
# Human Phenotype Ontology (HPO)

The Human Phenotype Ontology is a standardised ontology of phenotypic abnormalities. The EURO-NMD Registry adopts HPO for semiology (phenotype) definitions; its use was found to facilitate diagnostic research and gene discovery for rare diseases, including neuromuscular diseases.

stats.quote: The use of the Human Phenotype Ontology (HPO), particularly, was found to facilitate diagnostic research and gene discovery for rare diseases, including neuromuscular diseases.
Human phenotype ontology | Semiology definitions | https://hpo.jax.org/app/

extra.definition: The Human Phenotype Ontology (HPO) is a standardised ontology of phenotypic abnormalities, adopted by the EURO-NMD Registry for semiology (phenotype) definitions to make data machine-readable and interoperable.

hypercapnia.body:
# Hypercapnia

In DMD, hypercapnia first appears once MIP falls below ~30 cmH2O (or 30% predicted); MIP alone
best predicted its extent (log10 PaCO2 = -0.0026 x MIP% + 0.864).

extra.definition: Elevated arterial carbon-dioxide tension (defined in Hahn 1997 as PaCO2 > 6 kPa); a marker of ventilatory failure.

impaired-cough.body:
# Impaired cough

Progressively decreased cough efficacy is expected in DMD; guidelines trigger cough assistance
at PCF < 270 L/min or < 160 L/min, though Levine 2023 found PCF poorly correlated with severity.

extra.definition: Reduced cough effectiveness from expiratory-muscle weakness; PCF < 270 L/min is reduced and < 160 L/min is an ineffective cough.

inspiratory-reserve-volume.body:
# Inspiratory reserve volume (IRV)

MIP correlated strongly with IRV (r=0.83); later loss of IRV, VC and TLC reflects the
moderate, later-onset inspiratory-muscle deterioration in DMD.

stats.quote: declines did correlate linearly with inspiratory reserve volume (p < .001) and total lung capacity (p < .001)

extra.definition: The additional volume that can be inhaled above tidal inspiration (IRV); falls with inspiratory-muscle weakness in DMD.

isg15.body:
# ISG15

Reached gene-based significance for MG, but conditional analysis showed the only independent SNP
(rs3128125) lies in the neighbouring AGRN gene, so ISG15's signal is not independent.

stats.quote: ISG15 is located only 5.58 kb upstream of AGRN ... The only independent SNP (rs3128125) was in AGRN

extra.definition: ISG15 ubiquitin-like modifier on 1p36.33, 5.58 kb upstream of AGRN; gene-based-significant for MG but not independent of the AGRN signal.

late-onset-myasthenia-gravis.body:
# Late-onset myasthenia gravis (LOMG)

SNP heritability ~0.22. TNFRSF11A is the top non-HLA gene-based locus; HLA-DRB1 is the only
independent HLA locus, with HLA-DRB1*03:01 (and DRB1*13:01) protective.

stats.quote: in late-onset MG (LOMG; >=50 years old and particularly at >=60 years old) men are mostly affected

extra.definition: Anti-AChR MG with age at onset >= 50 years; male-predominant, with TNFRSF11A and HLA-DRB1 as the leading risk loci.

late-onset-vitiligo.body:
# Late-onset vitiligo (VLO)

Genetically correlated with MG (rg=0.33, p=0.03); the MG-VLO cross-disorder meta-analysis revealed
seven genome-wide-significant loci, including a novel ARID5B signal.

extra.definition: Late-onset vitiligo; an autoimmune depigmentation disorder genetically correlated with myasthenia gravis.

levine-2023-dmd-pft-severity.body:
# Levine 2023 — PFTs for DMD severity

Retrospective cross-sectional study (Schneider Children's Medical Center, Israel) of 90
DMD patients. FVC, TLC and transcutaneous CO2 correlated with age and ambulation and are
useful severity markers; peak cough flow (PCF) was randomly distributed and did not
correlate with severity.

extra.definition: Levine H, Goldfarb I, Katz J, et al. (2023), Acta Paediatrica 112:854-860, "Pulmonary function tests for evaluating the severity of Duchenne muscular dystrophy disease" — retrospective study of 90 DMD patients assessing which PFTs track disease severity.

linkage-disequilibrium-score-regression.body:
# LD-score regression (LDSC)

Used to confirm successful control of population stratification and to quantify MG's genetic
correlation with T1D, RA, ATD and late-onset vitiligo.

stats.quote: Genetic correlation analysis of MG with other autoimmune disorders was performed through LDSC

extra.definition: An LD-score-regression (LDSC) method estimating SNP heritability and cross-trait genetic correlation from GWAS summary statistics.

loss-of-ambulation.body:
# Loss of ambulation

Ambulatory status (ability to walk 10 m unassisted) stratifies DMD severity; FVC%, TLC% and
transcutaneous CO2 differ significantly between ambulatory and non-ambulatory patients.

extra.definition: Progressive inability to walk independently; in DMD typically occurring by age ~12 and used to stage disease severity.

lrp4.body:
# LRP4

Anti-LRP4 autoantibodies occur in double-seronegative and seropositive MG; LRP4 is the receptor
linking agrin to MuSK activation.

stats.quote: Lrp4 is a receptor for agrin and forms a complex with MuSK
an LRP4 interaction partner that mediates the activation of MuSK
the formation of AChR clusters in the postsynaptic membrane

extra.definition: Lipoprotein-receptor-related protein 4 (LRP4); the agrin receptor that complexes with MuSK to transduce agrin signalling at the neuromuscular junction.

maximal-expiratory-pressure.body:
# Maximal expiratory pressure (MEP)

Expiratory weakness (reduced MEP) is the first sign of respiratory-muscle dysfunction in DMD,
declining linearly with age; MEP is more severely affected than MIP across many neuromuscular
disorders.

stats.quote: reductions in expiratory muscle strength are the first signs of dysfunction and lead to the first episodes of respiratory failure
PFT values were lower for ... %MEP (p < 0.01 for all)

extra.definition: Maximal expiratory mouth pressure (MEP), measured after full inspiration; a readout of expiratory-muscle strength and the earliest respiratory abnormality in DMD.

maximal-inspiratory-pressure.body:
# Maximal inspiratory pressure (MIP)

Inspiratory strength is relatively preserved until ~13 years in DMD; once MIP falls below
~30 cmH2O (or 30% predicted), hypercapnia and chronic ventilatory insufficiency ensue.

stats.quote: we determined maximum inspiratory pressures (MIPs) ... as correlates of respiratory muscle strength
MIP alone best predicted the extent of hypercapnia

extra.definition: Maximal inspiratory mouth pressure (MIP), measured after full expiration; a readout of inspiratory-muscle (diaphragm) strength.

mayer-2015-dmd-pulmonary-function.body:
# Mayer 2015 — Pulmonary function in DMD

Prospective spirometry data (FVC and PEF) from 60 DMD patients (median age 10.3 y) in
the United Dystrophinopathy Project cohort at CHOP. Percent-predicted FVC and PEF
declined ~5%/year from ages 5-24; no difference by ambulation or steroid use. Proposes
modified ATS acceptability criteria for spirometry in neuromuscular disease.

extra.definition: Mayer OH et al. (2015), Pediatric Pulmonology 50:487-494, "Characterization of pulmonary function in Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy" — prospective natural-history spirometry (FVC, PEF) in 60 DMD patients with modified ATS acceptability criteria.

mechanical-ventilation.body:
# Mechanical ventilation

In Hahn 1997, 22 of 23 patients with MIP under 40% predicted required nocturnal assisted
ventilation; MIP/MEP help determine when ventilatory assistance is needed.

stats.quote: This predictably leads to the need for airway clearance and mechanical ventilation in the latter second to third decades

extra.definition: Invasive or non-invasive ventilatory support; initiated in DMD as respiratory-muscle failure produces nocturnal hypoventilation and ventilatory insufficiency.

mitochondrial-diseases.body:
# Mitochondrial Diseases

Mitochondrial diseases are one of the five main neuromuscular disease groups around which EURO-NMD is structured. In the EURO-NMD Registry they correspond to the "Mitochondrial Diseases" disease-driven dataset branch in REDCap; user feedback led to better mapping of variants of mitochondrial DNA in the registry's genetic diagnosis tools.

stats.quote: It is structured around five main disease groups: Muscle Diseases, Peripheral Nerve Diseases, Neuromuscular Junction Defects, Mitochondrial Diseases and Motor Neuron Diseases.
define five disease-driven datasets (Neuropathies, Myopathies, Mitochondrial Diseases, Neuromuscular Junction Disorders, and Motor Neuron Diseases).
five main disease groups: Muscle Diseases, Peripheral Nerve Diseases, Neuromuscular Junction Defects, Mitochondrial Diseases and Motor Neuron Diseases.

extra.definition: Mitochondrial diseases are one of the five main neuromuscular disease groups around which the EURO-NMD network and registry are structured, captured by a dedicated disease-driven dataset branch.

modified-ats-spirometry-criteria.body:
# Modified ATS spirometry acceptability criteria

Relax the standard ATS criteria (which maximise expiratory flow) to acknowledge respiratory-muscle
weakness, prioritising exhaled volume over expiratory force; enabled acceptable studies in 62% of
trials across ages 5-24.

stats.quote: we developed modified criteria for acceptability based on current ATS guidelines for spirometry acceptability
Using modified ATS criteria, curated spirometry data ... may provide a more reliable means of determining change in lung function over time

extra.definition: Mayer 2015's modified ATS acceptability criteria for spirometry in neuromuscular disease: no delay in onset of exhalation, clearly defined peak flow, termination at <=10% of peak flow, volume-time plateau (<25 mL change over final 1 s), FVC reproducibility within 10%, and no minimum forced expiratory time.

motor-neuron-diseases.body:
# Motor Neuron Diseases

Motor neuron diseases are one of the five main neuromuscular disease groups around which EURO-NMD is structured. In the EURO-NMD Registry they correspond to the "Motor Neuron Diseases" disease-driven dataset branch in REDCap, with their own disease-specific data elements and KPIs.

stats.quote: It is structured around five main disease groups: Muscle Diseases, Peripheral Nerve Diseases, Neuromuscular Junction Defects, Mitochondrial Diseases and Motor Neuron Diseases.
define five disease-driven datasets (Neuropathies, Myopathies, Mitochondrial Diseases, Neuromuscular Junction Disorders, and Motor Neuron Diseases).
five main disease groups: Muscle Diseases, Peripheral Nerve Diseases, Neuromuscular Junction Defects, Mitochondrial Diseases and Motor Neuron Diseases.

extra.definition: Motor neuron diseases are one of the five main neuromuscular disease groups around which the EURO-NMD network and registry are structured, captured by a dedicated disease-driven dataset branch.

mouse.body:
# Mouse (Mus musculus)

Agrin-deficient mice show defective neuromuscular synaptogenesis (fewer, smaller AChR clusters);
agrin immunisation induces MG-like disease — converging genetic and immunological evidence for
agrin's role at the neuromuscular junction.

stats.quote: immunisation of mice with agrin induces MG-like symptoms
agrin-deficient knockout mice have normal AChR levels but fewer postsynaptic clusters of reduced size and density

extra.definition: The laboratory mouse; used as a model to dissect agrin's role in acetylcholine-receptor clustering at the neuromuscular junction and to model myasthenia gravis.

muscle-diseases.body:
# Muscle Diseases (Myopathies)

Muscle diseases (myopathies) are one of the five main neuromuscular disease groups around which EURO-NMD is structured. In the EURO-NMD Registry they correspond to the "Myopathies" disease-driven dataset branch in REDCap, with their own disease-specific data elements and KPIs.

stats.quote: It is structured around five main disease groups: Muscle Diseases, Peripheral Nerve Diseases, Neuromuscular Junction Defects, Mitochondrial Diseases and Motor Neuron Diseases.
define five disease-driven datasets (Neuropathies, Myopathies, Mitochondrial Diseases, Neuromuscular Junction Disorders, and Motor Neuron Diseases).
five main disease groups: Muscle Diseases, Peripheral Nerve Diseases, Neuromuscular Junction Defects, Mitochondrial Diseases and Motor Neuron Diseases.

extra.definition: Muscle diseases (myopathies) are one of the five main neuromuscular disease groups around which the EURO-NMD network and registry are structured, captured by a dedicated disease-driven dataset branch.

muscle-weakness.body:
# Muscle weakness

In DMD, weakness is progressive and dystrophin-driven; in myasthenia gravis it is fatigable
and driven by autoantibody attack on the neuromuscular junction.

extra.definition: Reduced skeletal-muscle strength; a core feature of muscular dystrophies and of neuromuscular-junction disorders such as myasthenia gravis.

musk.body:
# MuSK

Anti-MuSK autoantibodies occur in up to 10% of MG patients; MuSK is the kinase hub of the
agrin-LRP4-MuSK pathway organising the postsynaptic apparatus.

stats.quote: Lrp4 is a receptor for agrin and forms a complex with MuSK
mediating MuSK activation and subsequent AChR clustering
the formation of AChR clusters in the postsynaptic membrane

extra.definition: Muscle-specific receptor tyrosine kinase (MuSK); activated by agrin via LRP4 to drive acetylcholine-receptor clustering at the neuromuscular junction.

myasthenia-gravis.body:
# Myasthenia gravis (MG)

Anti-AChR antibodies are detected in up to 85% of cases, anti-MuSK in up to 10%, with anti-LRP4,
anti-titin and anti-agrin in seronegative/seropositive cases. The HLA region carries the most
robust associations; gene-based analysis newly implicated AGRN. MG is genetically correlated
with T1D, RA, ATD and late-onset vitiligo, suggesting shared autoimmune pathways.

stats.quote: Myasthenia gravis (MG) is a rare autoimmune disorder affecting the neuromuscular junction (NMJ)
mediated by autoantibodies that target the postsynaptic proteins of the neuromuscular junction (NMJ), attenuating endplate potential and neuromuscular transmission
Muscle fatigue constitutes the typical feature of the disease
with ptosis, diplopia, bulbar and limb muscle weakness as typical clinical manifestations
with ptosis, diplopia, bulbar and limb muscle weakness as typical clinical manifestations
ptosis, diplopia, bulbar and limb muscle weakness as typical clinical manifestations
strong statistically significant genetic correlation between MG and type 1 diabetes (T1D) (rg=0.67, SE=0.13, p=4.78x10-7)
autoimmune thyroid disease (ATD) (rg=0.29, SE=0.11, p=0.0073)
late-onset vitiligo (VLO) (rg=0.33, SE=0.15, p=0.03)

extra.definition: A rare autoimmune disorder in which autoantibodies target postsynaptic proteins of the neuromuscular junction, attenuating neuromuscular transmission and causing fatigable muscle weakness; SNP heritability ~0.16.

neuromuscular-disorders.body:
# Neuromuscular disorders

Umbrella disease group structured by EURO-NMD into five areas: muscle diseases,
peripheral nerve diseases, neuromuscular junction defects, mitochondrial diseases and
motor neuron diseases. Duchenne muscular dystrophy, myasthenia gravis and spinal
muscular atrophy are members.

stats.quote: EURO-NMD is the European Reference Network for Rare Neuromuscular Diseases, collectively affecting 500,000 EU citizens

extra.definition: The group of rare disorders affecting muscle, peripheral nerve, the neuromuscular junction, mitochondria, or motor neurons; collectively affecting ~500,000 EU citizens.

neuromuscular-junction.body:
# Neuromuscular junction (NMJ)

Its postsynaptic membrane concentrates AChR clusters whose formation is organised by agrin-LRP4-MuSK
signalling; autoantibodies against these proteins cause myasthenia gravis. "Neuromuscular Junction
Defects" form one of EURO-NMD's five disease groups.

stats.quote: Pathogenic autoantibodies against the skeletal muscle acetylcholine receptor (AChR)

extra.definition: The chemical synapse between a motor neuron and skeletal muscle where acetylcholine drives muscle contraction; the autoimmune target in myasthenia gravis and the structure organised by agrin/LRP4/MuSK.

neuromuscular-junction-disorders.body:
# Neuromuscular Junction Disorders

Neuromuscular junction disorders (junction defects) are one of the five main neuromuscular disease groups around which EURO-NMD is structured, including diseases such as myasthenia gravis. In the EURO-NMD Registry they correspond to the "Neuromuscular Junction Disorders" disease-driven dataset branch in REDCap, with their own disease-specific data elements and KPIs.

stats.quote: It is structured around five main disease groups: Muscle Diseases, Peripheral Nerve Diseases, Neuromuscular Junction Defects, Mitochondrial Diseases and Motor Neuron Diseases.
a disease such as myasthenia gravis in comparison with a disease such as inclusion body myositis.
define five disease-driven datasets (Neuropathies, Myopathies, Mitochondrial Diseases, Neuromuscular Junction Disorders, and Motor Neuron Diseases).
five main disease groups: Muscle Diseases, Peripheral Nerve Diseases, Neuromuscular Junction Defects, Mitochondrial Diseases and Motor Neuron Diseases.

extra.definition: Neuromuscular junction disorders are one of the five main neuromuscular disease groups around which the EURO-NMD network and registry are structured, captured by a dedicated disease-driven dataset branch and including myasthenia gravis.

nmd-common-data-elements.body:
# NMD Common Data Elements (NMD-CDEs)

The NMD Common Data Elements are a common neuromuscular dataset of 44 fields, built on top of the EU-CDEs as the intersection of data elements chosen by all five disease areas (muscular, peripheral nerve, mitochondrial, neuromuscular junction and motor neuron diseases). They apply to any neuromuscular patient seen at a network node and form the cross-disease middle layer of the EURO-NMD Registry's dataset model.

stats.quote: a set of cross-neuromuscular data elements (NMD-CDEs).
a Common Neuromuscular Dataset of 44 fields serving all neuromuscular diseases (NMD-CDEs) ... It applies to any neuromuscular patient seen in a node of the network.
On top of the EU-CDEs, we have added a Common Neuromuscular Dataset of 44 fields serving all neuromuscular diseases (NMD-CDEs).

extra.definition: The NMD Common Data Elements (NMD-CDEs) are a common neuromuscular dataset of 44 fields representing the intersection of data elements chosen by all five EURO-NMD disease areas, applicable to any neuromuscular patient and forming the cross-disease layer of the EURO-NMD Registry.

nocturnal-hypoventilation.body:
# Nocturnal hypoventilation

When early respiratory failure is suspected in DMD, a full polysomnogram assesses for
nocturnal hypoventilation and often triggers initiation of ventilatory support.

extra.definition: Reduced alveolar ventilation during sleep; an early sign of respiratory failure in neuromuscular disease, assessed by polysomnography or transcutaneous CO2.

omim-database.body:
# OMIM Database

OMIM (Online Mendelian Inheritance in Man) is a knowledge base used for the classification of genes and diseases. It is one of the standard ontologies adopted by the EURO-NMD Registry for data integration and genetic diagnosis annotation.

stats.quote: OMIM | Classification of genes and diseases | https://www.omim.org
International classification of mutations (HGVS) (strongly recommended—see link)/HGNC/OMIM code.

extra.definition: OMIM (Online Mendelian Inheritance in Man) is a knowledge base for the classification of genes and diseases, adopted by the EURO-NMD Registry as one of its standard ontologies for data integration.

orphanet-rare-disease-ontology.body:
# Orphanet Rare Disease Ontology (ORDO)

The Orphanet Rare Disease Ontology is a structured vocabulary for classifying rare diseases. The EURO-NMD Registry links disease-name entries to ORDO codes for ontology search and validation, returning a list of codes for selection during data entry.

stats.quote: registry users can enter the name of a disease, and the system will return a list of codes from the Orphanet Rare Disease Ontology (ORDO) for selection.
ORDO (orphanet rare disease ontology) | Classification of rare diseases | https://www.orphadata.com/ordo/

extra.definition: The Orphanet Rare Disease Ontology (ORDO) is a structured vocabulary for the classification of rare diseases, used by the EURO-NMD Registry to validate and code disease entries during data entry.

peak-cough-flow.body:
# Peak cough flow (PCF)

Thresholds: > 270 L/min normal, < 160 L/min an ineffective cough. Levine 2023 found PCF
randomly distributed and uncorrelated with age, ambulation or steroid use, cautioning against
using PCF as the sole trigger for cough assistance.

stats.quote: Cough ability is assessed by peak cough flow (PCF), which is one of the most utilised measurements in the clinical evaluation of DMD
Peak cough flow values were randomly distributed and did not correlate with age, ambulation or treatment

extra.definition: The peak airflow generated by a maximal voluntary cough (PCF); used to gauge cough effectiveness and to time cough-assistance in neuromuscular disease.

peak-expiratory-flow.body:
# Peak expiratory flow (PEF)

Percent-predicted PEF declined ~5.8%/year (ages 5-24) and mirrored FVC; like FVC it showed no
significant difference by ambulation or steroid use in Mayer 2015.

stats.quote: assessment of PEF may also be helpful as a measure of disease progression in DMD since it assesses maximal expiratory effort as a surrogate measure for expiratory muscle strength

extra.definition: The maximal flow achieved during a forced exhalation (PEF); the most effort-dependent spirometric measure, used in DMD as a surrogate for expiratory-muscle strength.

peripheral-nerve-diseases.body:
# Peripheral Nerve Diseases (Neuropathies)

Peripheral nerve diseases (neuropathies) are one of the five main neuromuscular disease groups around which EURO-NMD is structured. In the EURO-NMD Registry they correspond to the "Neuropathies" disease-driven dataset branch in REDCap, with their own disease-specific data elements and KPIs.

stats.quote: It is structured around five main disease groups: Muscle Diseases, Peripheral Nerve Diseases, Neuromuscular Junction Defects, Mitochondrial Diseases and Motor Neuron Diseases.
define five disease-driven datasets (Neuropathies, Myopathies, Mitochondrial Diseases, Neuromuscular Junction Disorders, and Motor Neuron Diseases).
five main disease groups: Muscle Diseases, Peripheral Nerve Diseases, Neuromuscular Junction Defects, Mitochondrial Diseases and Motor Neuron Diseases.

extra.definition: Peripheral nerve diseases (neuropathies) are one of the five main neuromuscular disease groups around which the EURO-NMD network and registry are structured, captured by a dedicated disease-driven dataset branch.

postsynaptic-membrane.body:
# Postsynaptic membrane

Agrin-deficient mice have normal AChR levels but fewer, smaller postsynaptic clusters,
highlighting agrin as a critical organiser of postsynaptic differentiation.

stats.quote: the formation of AChR clusters in the postsynaptic membrane

extra.definition: The muscle-side membrane of the neuromuscular junction where acetylcholine receptors cluster; disrupted in myasthenia gravis.

prednisone.body:
# Prednisone / prednisolone

The most-used DMD glucocorticoid (83% of treated patients in Levine 2023).

stats.quote: The glucocorticoids most commonly used in DMD include prednisone/prednisolone and deflazacort
Daily glucocorticoid therapy (prednisone 0.75 mg/kg/day, maximum 30 mg/day ...) was recommended

extra.definition: A glucocorticoid (prednisone/prednisolone); the most commonly used corticosteroid regimen in DMD (0.75 mg/kg/day, max 30 mg/day).

progressive-muscle-atrophy.body:
# Progressive muscle atrophy

Dystrophin deficiency causes premature muscle-cell failure and progressive muscle atrophy,
producing weakness, loss of ambulation and respiratory decline.

extra.definition: Progressive loss of skeletal-muscle mass; in DMD a direct consequence of dystrophin deficiency.

ptosis.body:
# Ptosis

Together with diplopia, a typical early ocular manifestation of MG.

extra.definition: Drooping of the upper eyelid; a typical presenting ocular sign of myasthenia gravis.

ptpn22.body:
# PTPN22

Despite prior reports, this study found no support for a PTPN22 association with EOMG (rs2185827
p=0.06).

stats.quote: we did not find evidence supporting the previously reported implication of PTPN22 in EOMG

extra.definition: Protein tyrosine phosphatase non-receptor type 22 on 1p13.2; a classic autoimmune gene previously implicated in EOMG but not replicated here.

pulmonary-function-test.body:
# Pulmonary function test (PFT)

Serial PFTs (FVC, MIP/MEP, lung volumes, PCF, transcutaneous CO2) enable early identification
and treatment of respiratory complications in DMD.

stats.quote: Regular assessment of pulmonary function starting late in the first decade of life is part of the current standard of care in DMD

extra.definition: The panel of tests (spirometry, lung volumes, respiratory pressures, blood gases) used to monitor respiratory status; part of the DMD standard of care from late in the first decade.

redcap.body:
# REDCap

REDCap (Research Electronic Data Capture) is the secure web-based software used to collect and manage the EURO-NMD Registry data, hosted at University Medical Center Freiburg. It implements six disease-driven branches (Neuropathies, Myopathies, Mitochondrial Diseases, Neuromuscular Junction Disorders, Motor Neuron Diseases and undiagnosed patients), customised instruments, validation rules, an audit trail, and predefined data exports (CSV, SPSS, SAS, R, Stata, CDISC). The codebook is made available to users via the REDCap platform.

stats.quote: Data from the EURO-NMD Registry will be collected and managed using Research Electronic Data Capture (REDCap) software hosted at University Medical Center Freiburg.
These six subsets represent a "branch" of the Redcap data collection.

extra.definition: REDCap (Research Electronic Data Capture) is the secure web-based data-capture software, hosted at University Medical Center Freiburg, used to collect and manage data for the EURO-NMD Registry, with disease-driven branching, validation rules and predefined data exports.

residual-volume.body:
# Residual volume (RV)

As expiratory muscles weaken, ERV falls and RV rises; RV/TLC correlates strongly (inversely)
with MEP. RV% alone did not differ by ambulation in Levine 2023.

stats.quote: A strong correlation between expiratory muscle strength and RV became apparent when RV was expressed as a percentage of TLC

extra.definition: The volume remaining in the lungs after maximal expiration (RV); rises relative to TLC as expiratory muscles weaken.

respiratory-insufficiency.body:
# Respiratory (ventilatory) insufficiency

In DMD this develops during the second to third decade as respiratory muscles fail; the
patient loses the ability to inhale/exhale fully, cough effectively, and ventilate, leading
to airway-clearance needs and mechanical ventilation.

stats.quote: hypercapnia was present in 15 of 18 subjects with MIP values under 30cmH2O
leads to restrictive respiratory disease and added burden on the respiratory system

extra.definition: Chronic ventilatory (respiratory) insufficiency arising from progressive respiratory-muscle weakness in neuromuscular disease; heralded by falling vital capacity and culminating in hypercapnia and the need for assisted ventilation.

respiratory-muscle-weakness.body:
# Respiratory-muscle weakness

Expiratory muscle weakness (reduced MEP) appears first and earliest in DMD; inspiratory
weakness (reduced MIP) develops later but, once MIP falls below ~30 cmH2O, drives hypercapnia.

stats.quote: Respiratory insufficiency in DMD results from progressive respiratory muscle weakness that causes restrictive respiratory disease
inspiratory muscle dysfunction plays a key role in the development of chronic ventilatory insufficiency

extra.definition: Weakness of the inspiratory and expiratory muscles (diaphragm, intercostals, abdominals); the proximate driver of restrictive lung disease and respiratory failure in DMD.

respiratory-muscles.body:
# Respiratory muscles

Their strength is read out by MIP (inspiratory) and MEP (expiratory). In DMD, expiratory
weakness appears first; inspiratory weakness later governs CO2 retention.

extra.definition: The inspiratory (diaphragm, intercostals) and expiratory (abdominal) muscles whose progressive dystrophic weakness produces restrictive lung disease in DMD.

restrictive-lung-disease.body:
# Restrictive lung disease

The characteristic ventilatory defect of DMD: decreasing lung volume (vital/total lung
capacity) rather than airflow obstruction, tracked with FVC and TLC.

extra.definition: A restrictive respiratory pattern (reduced lung volumes/vital capacity) produced in DMD by progressive respiratory-muscle weakness, diaphragm involvement and thoracic-cage deformity.

rheumatoid-arthritis.body:
# Rheumatoid arthritis (RA)

Genetically correlated with MG (rg=0.5, p=3.83x10-5); HLA-DRB1*13:01 is protective in both MG and
anti-CCP-positive RA, hinting at shared mechanisms.

extra.definition: A chronic autoimmune inflammatory arthritis; genetically correlated with myasthenia gravis and a common comorbidity/familial autoimmune association.

rs231770.body:
# rs231770 (CTLA4)

The most significant CTLA4 SNP nearest the gene; CTLA4 reached significance in the gene-based MG
meta-analysis (p 1.43x10-6).

extra.definition: CTLA4 SNP associated with myasthenia gravis in the gene-based meta-analysis.

rs3128125.body:
# rs3128125 (AGRN)

Lies in one of six potential CTCF-binding sites in AGRN intron 2; functional effects on neuronal
agrin expression are not yet available via ENCODE.

stats.quote: rs3128125 is an intronic SNP which lies in the first quarter of the second, and largest, intron of AGRN

extra.definition: Intronic AGRN SNP (intron 2) and the only independent variant explaining the AGRN/ISG15 MG signal.

rs34481484.body:
# rs34481484 (HLA-DQA1)

The strongest HLA SNP in the overall MG GWAS meta-analysis.

stats.quote: An additional significantly associated locus was identified in the HLA-DQA1 gene (rs34481484 ...)

extra.definition: HLA-DQA1 SNP; the top and single genome-wide-significant HLA variant in the joint MG meta-analysis.

rs4369774.body:
# rs4369774 (TNFRSF11A)

The leading MG-associated SNP; also the top LOMG variant (OR 1.57, p 5.1x10-17).

stats.quote: Our top SNP (rs4369774 ...) is in an intron of the tumour necrosis factor receptor superfamily member 11A (TNFRSF11A) gene

extra.definition: Intronic TNFRSF11A SNP; the top genome-wide-significant variant in the overall MG meta-analysis.

scoliosis.body:
# Scoliosis

In the Hahn 1997 cohort, increasing scoliosis (>50°) accompanied advancing age; it stiffens
the thoracic cage and can lower FVC independently of muscle strength.

extra.definition: Lateral curvature of the spine; common in non-ambulatory DMD and a confounder of FVC measurement.

skeletal-muscle.body:
# Skeletal muscle

Progressive dystrophic deterioration of skeletal muscle (including respiratory muscles)
underlies the restrictive ventilatory defect of DMD.

extra.definition: Striated voluntary muscle tissue; the site of dystrophic deterioration in DMD and of acetylcholine-receptor-directed autoimmune attack at the neuromuscular junction in myasthenia gravis.

smartcare-registry.body:
# SMArtCARE Registry

SMArtCARE is one of the four pilot registries (a clinical registry) made interoperable with the EURO-NMD Registry. It is associated with spinal muscular atrophy, for which costly disease-modifying treatments prompted additional data collection capturing clinical progression and treatment response. It participated in the proof-of-concept federated queries of the EURO-NMD Registry Hub.

stats.quote: data from the EURO-NMD registry is now interoperable with four existing pilot registries: Duchenne Data Platform, CRAMP, DM-SCope and SMArtCARE.
the recent marketing approval of often costly disease-modifying treatments in several neuromuscular disorders, e.g., Spinal Muscular Atrophy, additional data collection ... has been initiated.
Conducting queries related to neuromuscular diseases is possible without exposing sensitive patient details.
interoperable with four existing pilot registries: Duchenne Data Platform, CRAMP, DM-SCope and SMArtCARE.

extra.definition: SMArtCARE is a clinical neuromuscular registry, associated with spinal muscular atrophy, made interoperable with the EURO-NMD Registry as one of four pilot registries demonstrating the EURO-NMD Registry Hub federation framework.

spinal-muscular-atrophy.body:
# Spinal muscular atrophy (SMA)

A motor-neuron-disease group member; the SMArtCARE registry (interoperable with EURO-NMD)
captures SMA data, and SMA exemplifies post-marketing registries for costly disease-modifying
therapies.

stats.quote: additional data collection that better captures clinical progression and response to treatment has been initiated, e.g., Spinal Muscular Atrophy
MEP has been found to be more severely affected than MIP in ... the spinal muscular atrophies

extra.definition: A motor-neuron neuromuscular disorder; like other neuromuscular diseases it shows early, severe expiratory-muscle (MEP) weakness, and is a target of recent disease-modifying therapies.

spirometry.body:
# Spirometry

Acceptable spirometry could be obtained in 50-71% of attempts across ages 5-24 using modified
ATS criteria; acceptability fell with age as ambulation was lost.

stats.quote: A maximal expiratory maneuver ... is required to properly perform spirometry and produce an accurate FVC
Spirometry is a widely used and fairly easily performed technique to assess lung function, and in particular lung volume
spirometry could be performed reliably in subjects with DMD

extra.definition: A forced expiratory maneuver (full inspiration then maximal exhalation) producing FVC and PEF; effort-dependent and challenging in respiratory-muscle weakness.

srcap.body:
# SRCAP

A subunit of the SRCAP chromatin-remodelling complex important in haematopoiesis (lymphoid lineage
fate) and muscle differentiation; novel EOMG locus (independent SNP rs8058928).

stats.quote: we detected a novel genome-wide significant association with EOMG at a region that lies between the SRCAP and FBRS genes

extra.definition: Snf2-related CREBBP activator protein on 16p11.2; site of a novel early-onset MG association in the SRCAP-FBRS region.

time-to-diagnosis.body:
# Time to Diagnosis

Time to diagnosis is a key performance indicator (KPI) used by the EURO-NMD Registry to benchmark healthcare provider processes across all neuromuscular diseases. It is not directly captured but derived at cohort level from the date of the patient's first contact with the expert centre together with the confirmed molecular diagnosis and the diagnosis date.

stats.quote: Across all neuromuscular diseases, "time to diagnosis" and "time to treatment" were identified as KPIs enabling comparing processes at different HCPs.
the KPIs are not directly captured by the registry but are derived indicators that can be generated from data elements at a cohort level.
"time to diagnosis" can be derived from the date of a patient's first coming to the attention of the expert centre, together with the confirmed molecular diagnosis and the date of the diagnosis.

extra.definition: Time to diagnosis is a key performance indicator derived by the EURO-NMD Registry from the date of a patient's first contact with the expert centre and the date of confirmed molecular diagnosis, used to benchmark healthcare providers across all neuromuscular diseases.

time-to-treatment.body:
# Time to Treatment

Time to treatment is a key performance indicator (KPI) used by the EURO-NMD Registry to compare healthcare-provider processes across neuromuscular diseases. It captures the average time from a patient's first contact with the healthcare provider to the start of targeted therapy and, like other KPIs, is derived from registry data elements at cohort level rather than captured directly.

stats.quote: Across all neuromuscular diseases, "time to diagnosis" and "time to treatment" were identified as KPIs enabling comparing processes at different HCPs.
Average time from the patient's first contact with HCP to diagnosis or start of targeted therapy.
"time to diagnosis" and "time to treatment" were identified as KPIs enabling comparing processes at different HCPs.

extra.definition: Time to treatment is a key performance indicator derived by the EURO-NMD Registry to compare the average time from a patient's first contact with the healthcare provider to the start of targeted therapy across centres and neuromuscular diseases.

titin.body:
# Titin

Anti-titin antibodies are among the striated-muscle autoantibodies detected in MG, though
anti-titin screening was not performed in all cases in this study.

stats.quote: striated muscle proteins, such as titin

extra.definition: A giant striated-muscle sarcomeric protein; a striated-muscle autoantigen against which antibodies are detected in some MG patients.

tnfrsf11a.body:
# TNFRSF11A (RANK)

Encodes a TNF-receptor-family member on antigen-presenting dendritic cells; its deficiency in
mice impairs negative T-cell selection and produces autoimmunity. Top non-HLA gene-based locus
for LOMG, not associated with EOMG.

stats.quote: We confirmed the previously reported MG association with TNFRSF11A (rs4369774; p=1.09x10-13, OR=1.4)
LOMG gene-based association analysis (excluding the HLA region) revealed TNFRSF11A as the only genome-wide significant locus

extra.definition: TNF receptor superfamily member 11A (RANK) on 18q21.33; a confirmed myasthenia gravis risk gene, particularly for late-onset MG.

tnip1.body:
# TNIP1

Previously mapped to a Pro151Ala change implicated in EOMG; in this larger meta-analysis it only
reached p=5.93x10-6 (below genome-wide significance).

stats.quote: the previously reported association with TNIP1 only reached a p value of 5.93x10-6

extra.definition: TNFAIP3-interacting protein 1 on 5q33.1; previously reported in EOMG but only nominally associated in this study.

topaloudi-2022-myasthenia-gravis-gwas.body:
# Topaloudi 2022 — Myasthenia gravis GWAS

Largest MG GWAS meta-analysis to date. Confirms TNFRSF11A and HLA associations, and via
gene-based analysis newly implicates AGRN — the first MG risk gene encoding a protein
(agrin) directly relevant to the neuromuscular junction. Reveals distinct EOMG vs LOMG
genetic architecture and genetic correlation of MG with T1D, RA, ATD and late-onset
vitiligo.

extra.definition: Topaloudi A et al. (2022), J Med Genet 59:801-809, "Myasthenia gravis genome-wide association study implicates AGRN as a risk locus" — GWAS meta-analysis of 1401 MG cases and 3508 controls with HLA fine-mapping, onset-specific (EOMG/LOMG) and cross-autoimmune genetic-correlation analyses.

total-lung-capacity.body:
# Total lung capacity (TLC)

Percent-predicted TLC fell ~5.5%/year in non-ambulatory DMD and, like FVC, correlated with age
and ambulation, supporting its use as a prognostic severity marker.

stats.quote: Significant annual declines were demonstrated among nonambulatory patients, in ... total lung capacity (5.5%) per year
PFT values were lower for ... %TLC ... (p < 0.01)

extra.definition: The total volume of air in the lungs after maximal inspiration (TLC); a lung-volume marker of restrictive disease in DMD.

transcutaneous-co2.body:
# Transcutaneous CO2 (PtcCO2)

Higher in non-ambulatory than ambulatory DMD patients (p=0.04) and rising with age in
non-ambulatory patients (r=0.55), supporting it as a severity/follow-up marker.

stats.quote: This measurement was found to be a prognostic parameter, also for night hypoventilation status
transcutaneous carbon dioxide measurement correlated significantly with age (r = 0.55, p = 0.02)

extra.definition: Non-invasive transcutaneous measurement of carbon-dioxide tension (PtcCO2); a prognostic marker of (night-time) hypoventilation in DMD.

type-1-diabetes.body:
# Type 1 diabetes (T1D)

Genetically correlated with MG (rg=0.67, p=4.78x10-7; rg=0.73 with HLA excluded), the strongest
correlation among 13 autoimmune disorders tested.

extra.definition: Autoimmune destruction of pancreatic beta cells; the autoimmune disorder most strongly genetically correlated with myasthenia gravis.

udp-cohort.body:
# United Dystrophinopathy Project (UDP) cohort

Prospective DMD natural-history cohort (2005-2010, CHOP) enrolling English-speaking patients
with a DMD phenotype and confirmed dystrophin mutation; 60 subjects contributed spirometry.

stats.quote: part of an Institutional Review Board approved United Dystrophinopathy Project (UDP) genotype-phenotype cohort study

extra.definition: The United Dystrophinopathy Project (UDP) genotype-phenotype cohort study at CHOP; source of the prospective DMD spirometry data in Mayer 2015.

vamorolone.body:
# Vamorolone

A corticosteroid under investigation; used in 2 of 53 corticosteroid-treated DMD patients in
Levine 2023.

stats.quote: 2/53 (3.8%) with vamorolone
Vamorolone—Corticosteroid under investigation

extra.definition: A dissociative corticosteroid (investigational at the time of Levine 2023) used in a minority of DMD patients.

vital-capacity.body:
# Vital capacity (VC)

VC% best correlated with age (r=-0.80) among thoracic volumes; plateau VC >2.5 L predicted slow
subsequent decline (~4.1%/yr) versus <1.7 L (~9.6%/yr).

stats.quote: the percentage of predicted normal VC decreased at the linear rate of 7.9% per year until age 20
the extent of the plateau-phase VC was found to correlate with life expectancy and the descending-phase rate of decline to correlate with the risk of respiratory failure

extra.definition: The maximal volume exhaled after maximal inspiration (VC); in DMD it follows ascending, plateau and descending phases, and the plateau value predicts life expectancy.

world-duchenne-organisation.body:
# World Duchenne Organisation

The World Duchenne Organisation is one of three patient organisations that co-funded the EURO-NMD Registry Hub and contributed in-kind support. Focused on the Duchenne muscular dystrophy community, it acted as an equal partner with co-governance rights in the registry's co-design.

stats.quote: The EURO-NMD Registry Hub project has been supported by three patient organisations, AFM-Téléthon, Duchenne Data Foundation, and World Duchenne Organisation.
three leading patient organisations, World Duchenne Organisation, Duchenne Data Foundation and AFM-Téléthon.
co-funding from the EU 3rd Health Programme and three leading patient organisations, World Duchenne Organisation, Duchenne Data Foundation and AFM-Téléthon.

extra.definition: The World Duchenne Organisation is a patient organisation that co-funded and provided in-kind contributions to the EURO-NMD Registry Hub project, supporting its patient-centred design.

zbtb10.body:
# ZBTB10

A previously reported LOMG locus (Seldin et al.) for which this larger meta-analysis found no
supporting evidence (rs381550 p=0.02, gene-based p=0.14).

stats.quote: we did not find evidence supporting the previously reported implication of ... ZBTB10 in LOMG

extra.definition: Zinc finger and BTB domain containing 10 on 8q21.13; previously reported in LOMG but not replicated in this study.
